title: Fisetin Fights Frailty: New Study Shows Supplment Preserves Strength
abstract: A new study published in *Aging Cell* delves into the exciting findings surrounding fisetin’s impact on physical function and cellular aging in mice. > “Our findings suggest that treatment with fisetin may be a viable therapeutic approach to improve physical function and reduce excess cell senescence in skeletal muscle with aging.”. This finding is highly significant because it suggests that fisetin, a natural compound, can be as effective as more targeted or synthetic approaches in improving age-related physical function. (Murray et al., 2025) **Fisetin Is Comparable to Powerful Senolytics.** There are no statistically significant differences between the efficacy of fisetin, genetic removal of senescent cells (GCV), and ABT-263 when it comes to reducing frailty and increasing grip strength. While this study primarily focused on muscle and physical function, the same research group showed that intermittent supplementation with fisetin improves arterial function in old mice. S. Intermittent Supplementation With Fisetin Improves Physical Function and Decreases Cellular Senescence in Skeletal Muscle With Aging: A Comparison to Genetic Clearance of Senescent Cells and Synthetic Senolytic Approaches.
